methodology: Limited ten-ayah first pass. Earlier textual comparisons checked against displayed Hebrew Masoretic passages and modern critical translation, not a full witness/philology audit. Absence of identified parallel is not absence proof.

verses.note: Scripture-recitation and belief: preliminary pass; no passage-specific earlier textual link established.
Israelite remembrance of favor: generic covenant exhortation; no specific earlier source established.
Judgment and intercession: broad eschatological motif, not a traceable parallel at this depth.
Abraham tested and appointed leader, covenant not extending to wrongdoers; compare Genesis 17:1–14, which differs in covenant scope and stipulations.
Sanctuary and Abraham's station: Genesis 12:7–8 depicts Abraham building altars in Canaan, not a Kaaba foundation or Meccan sanctuary.
Abraham's prayer for secure city and provision: no exact earlier narrative established.
Abraham and Ishmael raising foundations of the House: Genesis 12:7–8 depicts Abraham alone at Canaanite altars, not Abraham and Ishmael constructing the Kaaba.
Abraham and Ishmael pray for submission and a community: no precise primary-text parallel established.
Prayer for messenger teaching scripture: no exact pre-Qur'anic episode identified.
Abraham's religious way and divine election: broad ancestral faith motif; no specific episode established.

candidates.edition: Sefaria Hebrew Masoretic text; Revised JPS 2023 English
candidates.similarity: Both associate Abraham with divine instruction and a covenant extending to descendants.
candidates.difference: Genesis specifies circumcision, land of Canaan and generational covenant; Qur'an 2:124 emphasizes tested commands, Abraham as imam and exclusion of wrongdoers.
candidates.caveat: Different covenant emphases; not a direct quotation, and no demonstrated literary dependence.

candidates.edition: Sefaria Hebrew Masoretic text; Revised JPS 2023 English
candidates.similarity: Abraham is connected with construction of a worship site.
candidates.difference: Genesis describes Abraham's altars at Shechem and near Bethel in Canaan, without Ishmael or Mecca; Qur'an names the House and, in 2:127, Abraham with Ishmael.
candidates.caveat: Do not equate altar-building with construction of the Kaaba or claim that Genesis documents Meccan history.

open_questions: Investigate pre-Islamic witnesses for Abraham/Ishmael and Mecca without retrojecting later Muslim accounts.
Distinguish Genesis composition/redaction from surviving manuscripts and modern translations.
Evaluate Q2:124 with Genesis 17 and alternative covenant interpretations before publication.
